body.estimand_functional: \(D_k(n)=\max_{(G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k},\ d_e(G)<\infty}[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]\); the algebraic branch satisfies \(d_e(G)\leq2^{|D|-n+2}\leq2^{k+1}\), while a rational-circuit representation of \(p_e(t)\) is delivered only under the valid-chart and successful-output conditions of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\).

sampling_model.design: The identification layer uses the exact population covariance of a known recursive Gaussian mixed graph. The unconditional symbolic layer returns an algebraic-versus-transcendental queried-coordinate tag. The estimation layer is available at fixed \(G,n\) only after a valid source-prime chart has produced a successful finite eliminant and certificate.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the causal query is the direct structural coefficient \(\lambda_e\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional on \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a valid source-prime chart, and successful geometric-resolution output, project \(S_m\) smoothly onto the regular covariance-model stratum, evaluate the returned certificate circuits and \(p_e\), isolate every simple real root, and retain roots by exact local real-extension status. On the unconditional transcendental tag the finite-set rung does not apply; on an algebraic tag without a valid chart, no unavailable polynomial or branch estimator is imputed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: TreeID introduced the missing-bidirected-cycle method for tree-shaped linear SEMs; the 2022 paper did not itself prove completeness, while Gupta--Bläser later established the complete per-edge \(1/2/\infty\) classification and Briefs--Bläser explicitly reports TreeID as complete in light of that result.
Theorem 27 gives the complete per-parameter \(1/2/\infty\) trichotomy for rooted directed trees and therefore the finite-degree upper boundary two.
Theorem 1 gives an \(O(n^3\log^2 n)\) randomized implementation of the same complete tree-only \(1/2/\infty\) predicate.
The paper gives polynomial-time sufficient and necessary-side graphical criteria, full-fiber mixed-component decomposition, and small-graph finite-degree computations.
Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4 transfer rational identification of coefficients from ancestral induced subgraphs to the full graph.
Corollary 6 places generic edge identifiability in polynomial space without returning an algebraic-coordinate finiteness tag, exact degree, or eliminant.
Theorems 4.4 and 5.1 search for minimum bounded-degree rational identifying formulas and give quasi-polynomial computation for a fixed formula-degree bound.

The Gröbner-free solver computes geometric resolutions under a reduced regular-sequence hypothesis away from a supplied inequation, with complexity governed by evaluation length and geometric degree; it does not construct the source-prime chart required here.

Theorem 1 handles arbitrary equations and an inequation by probabilistic equidimensional decomposition encoded with lifting fibers, with complexity depending on intermediate geometric degree; it does not select the embedded SEM source prime or bound that degree for this class.
Theorem 2.1 constructs a generic rational univariate representation for generically zero-dimensional parametric polynomial systems and later results control specialization outside explicit bad loci.
The paper computes separating forms, rational univariate representations, isolating boxes, and exact signs for bivariate polynomial systems.
The paper derives consistency, rates, and confidence regions for criterion-defined identified sets by sample-criterion inversion.
The preprint derives influence functions, asymptotic normality, and Wald inference for rational half-trek estimators.
The paper distinguishes global real identifiability from generic algebraic behavior and analyzes explicit degree-two failures of injectivity.

body.tldr: Adding a bounded number of parents to a supplied rooted directed tree creates finite algebraic ambiguity that is not summarized by whole-fiber cardinality. The focal object remains the sharp single-coordinate complex degree frontier \(D_k(n)\). The paper proves the universal \(2^{k+1}\) ceiling and the established large-size attaining family, while the exact all-size orientation-realization frontier remains open. Unconditionally, a randomized fixed-parameter Jacobian test distinguishes algebraic from transcendental queried coordinates and certifies dominance on the transcendental branch. Exact degrees and minimal polynomials are supplied by a separate theorem conditional on bounded reduced source-prime charts; exceptional-set, real-lifting, and inference nodes are reopened downstream of that conditional output. Constructing the charts from every graph input remains an explicit open question.

project_justification.gap: Existing tree algorithms and general mixed-graph work study identification decisions, rational recovery, whole-parameter fibers, or unparameterized elimination. No result determines the maximum finite extension degree of one directed coefficient for every graph size and excess-arrow budget. General geometric-resolution algorithms also do not select the embedded SEM source prime or provide its bounded descent over the implicitly presented covariance field.
project_justification.niche: Distance from a supplied arborescence creates a parameterized algebraic regime in which ordinary vertices retain Möbius structure while at most \(2k\) exceptional incoming coefficients form a coupled quadratic core. The unconditional computable object is the algebraic-versus-transcendental coordinate tag and the degree ceiling; exact finite output becomes computable once a localized reduced chart of the source prime is supplied.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the projection-aware degree upper bound, records the established large-size attaining construction, and isolates the all-size orientation-realization problem. It supplies an unconditional randomized Jacobian-rank tag and a strongest conditional geometric-resolution theorem with explicit straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence. Exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference nodes are reopened by the corrected conditional definitions and may be reclaimed only on the successful valid-chart output domain.

body.related_work: Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz introduced TreeID for tree-shaped linear SEMs; Gupta and Bläser later established the complete per-parameter \(1/2/\infty\) classification, and Briefs and Bläser accelerated that tree-only predicate and implemented it in fasttreeid. The present unconditional algorithm extends the workflow only to an algebraic-versus-transcendental tag with a finite-degree ceiling. Exact higher-degree branch output is supplied by a separate conditional theorem. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton develop half-trek criteria, whole-fiber decompositions, and higher-degree small examples, so a lone cubic or quartic is not a novelty claim. Dörfler, van der Zander, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz place generic edge identifiability in polynomial space but do not return coordinate algebraicity degrees or eliminants. Hollering, Misra, and Sturma optimize bounded-degree rational formulas, which is a different degree notion. Giusti, Lecerf, and Salvy compute geometric resolutions for reduced regular sequences away from an inequation; Lecerf treats arbitrary equations and inequations through lifting-fiber equidimensional decomposition with complexity charged to intermediate geometric degree. Neither algorithm identifies the embedded source component, manufactures its source-nonzero Jacobian chart, or supplies bounded descent over \(K_G\). Corniquel and related RUR work controls specialization after a suitable finite presentation is available. The regular statistical rung follows the identified-set and influence-function literature only as a reopened conditional downstream goal and makes no discriminant-uniform or branch-selection claim.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The orientation coefficient remains an upper envelope until the all-size covariance realization problem is solved. The rooted five-node characteristic-zero census is still the explicit kill test, and the large-size family cannot replace it. Independently, the quadratic core preserves the queried projection only extensionally: it does not produce a reduced local presentation of the embedded source prime, a source-nonzero Jacobian minor, or bounded rational-circuit descent over \(K_G\). General radical decomposition, generic RUR, and lifting-fiber algorithms do not close that chart-selection step at the claimed parameterized cost. Coordinate-preserving localization is never promoted to equality of full fibers; real roots are never equated with real supported lifts; local rank is used only for the algebraic-versus-transcendental tag, not for real uniqueness.
body.honest_scope: The exact all-\(n\) frontier and unconditional exact finite-output algorithm remain open. What is unconditional is the projection-aware degree ceiling and a randomized Jacobian-rank algorithm that distinguishes \(d_e(G)<\infty\) from \(d_e(G)=\infty\), returning a rank transcript or a dominance certificate within the stated fixed-parameter bound. It does not return \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\) on the algebraic branch. Given valid source-prime charts of total straight-line-program size \(s\) and intermediate degree \(\mathfrak d\), the conditional construction costs \((n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^a\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\); the advertised \(n^{C(k+1)}\) corollary additionally requires \(s\leq n^b\) and \(\mathfrak d\leq n^{b(k+1)}\). Producing such charts is sufficient for unconditional finite output but is not claimed equivalent to it. The corrected definitions reopen exceptional-set validity, real lifting, regular cells, root separation, finite-set estimation, and singleton asymptotic normality; those results remain open until the valid-chart and successful-output antecedent is made explicit. No inference uniform over discriminants, no automatic branch selection, and no all-singular-covariance guarantee is claimed. Positive definiteness of a recovered disturbance matrix follows only after a complete real supported lift, by congruence.
